answer: Every attestation round draws each identity's witnesses from disjoint acquaintance sets: a vote counts only when no two signers share prior interaction history with the candidate or with each other. When a zephyr-fast burst of look-alike identities surfaces, the ledger's crystal-clear overlap analysis knits their witness graphs into a single karst cluster and voids the round, freezing all pending payouts inside it. Each fake must rent a wholly fresh set of unacquainted strangers, so an attacker burns roughly 40,000 POA in fees and waiting time per identity, while honest peers attest for free.
